subject: Regional egress latency — mitigation plan and customer routing instructions
messages:
From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@acme-fin.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, dylan_brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 May 2028 09:12:03 -0700
Subject: [Redwood] Notice: elevated egress latency affecting US-east and EU-west — immediate guidance

Samir,

Thanks for the quick heads-up on the increased tail latency you saw this morning. We’ve opened an incident and our SREs are actively investigating a networking egress degradation that is intermittently affecting requests originating from our US-east and EU-west cloud peering paths. At a high level: 

- Scope: ~6% of requests to hosted inference in US-east and ~4% in EU-west show elevated egress latency (200–800ms extra) starting ~08:40 UTC.
- Impact: increased LLM response latency and occasional timeouts for longer sequences. No data loss.
- Immediate mitigation: we recommend customers temporarily prefer alternate region endpoints (us-west or eu-north) using regional routing headers while we validate a fix. See suggested routing headers below.

Suggested short-term header-based override for your client (example):
- X-Redwood-Prefer-Region: us-west
- X-Redwood-Prefer-Region: eu-north

I’ve attached a quick snapshot of token-level latency (egress_latency_snapshot.csv) and will follow up with a concrete reroute patch once SRE confirms. If you can route a small percentage of traffic to us-west for validation, we’ll monitor closely and coordinate.

Apologies for the disruption — we’ll share continuous updates.

— Laura Bennett
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Attachment: egress_latency_snapshot.csv (CSV summary, 5 rows)

From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@acme-fin.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: platform-ops@pinnaclehealth.io
Date: Wed, 22 May 2028 09:28:50 -0700
Subject: Re: [Redwood] Notice: elevated egress latency affecting US-east and EU-west — immediate guidance

Thanks Laura — we started seeing the spike in our synthetic checks around 08:50 UTC. We can fail a small percentage (10%) of traffic to us-west for testing. Two quick asks:
1) What level of request affinity will change when we shift region? We want to avoid session fragmentation for long chats.
2) Can you confirm if model versions are identical in the fallback regions?

Samir
Senior Platform Engineer, Acme Financial
samir.khan@acme-fin.com

From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 May 2028 09:35:12 -0700
Subject: Fwd: [Redwood] Notice: elevated egress latency — customer routing coordination

Internal: Samir wants confirmation on affinity and model parity. Quick notes for the SRE/infra team before we reply to the customer: 
- Affinity: session affinity is token-prefix based and preserved when routing within the same model family and compatible runtime. If we send to a different region running the same pinned model version, affinity should hold for active sessions; clients that are connection-bound to a region will see a new connection but tokens remain coherent via KV cache forwarding.
- Model parity: most curated models are mirrored across regions; we need to confirm the specific model build numbers for Acme’s pinned model (acme-fin-v1). Dylan, can you confirm mirror build hash and whether any quantization differences apply?

I’ll hold the customer on the 10% test until we have confirmation. Vivek — I’m looping you in so leadership is aware in case Acme escalates to procurement.

— Marissa
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: dylan_brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Samir Khan <samir.khan@acme-fin.com>
Date: Wed, 22 May 2028 10:02:21 -0700
Subject: Re: [Redwood] Notice: elevated egress latency — model parity & patch for routing

Samir / team — technical update: 
- Model parity: Acme’s pinned model acme-fin-v1 is mirror-synced. Build hash: b7a4f3e; same quantization profile across us-east/us-west/eu-north. No regression expected when routing.
- Affinity: confirmed — session tokens will rehydrate via KV cache transfer; clients should maintain conversational context after reroute.
- Proposed hotfix: we will push a transient routing rule at the edge to prefer alternate peering for affected prefixes and open a short-lived HTTP header override for customers who want explicit control. Patch attached (route_patch.diff).
- Rollout plan: 1) deploy edge rule to 5% of traffic in 10 minutes; 2) monitor error/latency metrics for 15 minutes; 3) expand to 50% if stable; 4) remove when peering heals.

I’ll kick off step 1 now and update the incident page.

— Dylan Brooks
Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: route_patch.diff

From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@acme-fin.com>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 May 2028 10:18:44 -0700
Subject: Re: [Redwood] Notice: elevated egress latency — model parity & patch for routing

Thanks Dylan — please proceed with the rollout. We’ve flipped 10% to us-west and initial checks look good (p95 latency back to normal). Please keep the team posted before you expand to 50%. Also please include an ETA for full remediation so we can update our incident timeline internally.

Samir

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@acme-fin.com>, dylan_brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 23 May 2028 07:40:00 -0700
Subject: [Redwood] Incident update: mitigation successful, postmortem draft and next steps

Team / Samir — follow-up: 
- Status: edge routing change reduced affected traffic to under 0.5% across both regions; us-east peering partner is applying a backend fix with an estimated completion in ~18 hours.
- Customer impact: reduced to intermittent single-digit errors for long sequences. We recommend keeping the header override in place for mission-critical flows until the partner confirms complete heal.
- Postmortem: draft available here https://drive.redwood.example/postmortems/2028-05-egress-draft (redwood_postmortem_draft.pdf attached).

Action items: 
1) Ops: confirm partner fix and request post-fix connectivity test (Dylan).
2) CS: coordinate customer credit/communication (Marissa).
3) Sales/AM: notify procurement contacts if Acme requests contract remediation (Vivek).

We’ll send a final closure note after partner validation.

— Laura

Attachment: redwood_postmortem_draft.pdf

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@acme-fin.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, dylan_brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 24 May 2028 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Redwood] Incident closure: regional egress latency — final notes and remediation plan

Samir — quick closing note and next steps from our side: 

1) Final status: partner applied fix at 03:40 UTC this morning; monitored for ~24 hours with normal p95/p99. No further customer-visible regressions reported.
2) Customer credit: Marissa will follow up with a proposed credit based on impacted token volume and our SLA terms.
3) Engineering remediation: we will add a persistent health probe on the impacted peering path and an automated short-circuit that flips to alternate peering at 90th percentile latency >300ms for 5 min. ETA for rollout: 3 weeks (RI-4523).
4) Postmortem: we’ve posted the final doc and invited Acme to a 30-min readout/QA session next week. Link: https://drive.redwood.example/postmortems/2028-05-egress-final

Apologies again for the disruption and thank you and your team for working closely with us on the temporary routing. Please let Marissa know preferred times for the readout.

— Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
